# Review — secret-history-125-130 (§§125–130)

Reviewer pass 1 and pass 2. Severity: major = wrong grammar or sense against the text; moderate = a label, voice, convention or invented content that would mislead a reader; minor = loose, inconsistent with the published parts or the glossary; trivial = wording.

## Counts

- Pass 1: 131 changes: major 0, moderate 61, minor 58, trivial 12
- Pass 2: 24 changes: major 0, moderate 3, minor 20, trivial 1

Pass 1 counts one change per unit and field; the four whole-part sweeps (names in l, qan → Qan, anda gloss, amu- lemma) are counted per unit but listed on one row each below.

## Pass 2 — units.json header and morph, gloss.json

Gloss coverage: 134 novel forms, 134 keys, none missing, none unused; 13 `__broaden__` entries each begin with the old entry whole + " · " (checked by script).

## Findings refused (with reason)

- U23 i 'why did you not make…': a first thought was to change 'why' to 'how' to match the note. Refused: the glossary renders jakin 'how, why'; the note now says 'how, why'.
- U33 helige: considered forcing 'liver' (the glossary's helige). Refused: the Ming gives 伏臥 'lying prone' for the whole word and the note already says helige is 'liver' elsewhere; kept uncertain.
- U9 i 'will they not be mine, you?' reads awkwardly. Refused: boluγ̇užai has no stated complement and the ending is unknown; the note already says the whole speech is uncertain; any smoother English would invent a sense.
- U13 i supplies 'To'oril Qan said:' and the opening mark. Kept (the Ming gives no break); the note now says these are the translator's.
- U12 / glossary daγai: Daqai (printed D) vs Taqai in 121–124. Refused to unify the spellings in i (each is the plain spelling of what Shiratori prints); the note flags the probable identity.
- U39 Külelkü = Kürelkü of §123: not equated in the unit or note (identity unverifiable from the text); only hedged ('perhaps the same') in the gloss entry.
- U42 i 'drove Chinggis Qahan back there': 'back' is slightly more than ködülge- 'set in motion, drive off'. Left; mild and tied to the uncertain stem already flagged.
- U37 i 'banded together' for nököčežü, 'those headed by him' for teriġüten: kept as readings; the stem and the suffix are flagged uncertain in morph and glossary (teriġüten now broadened).
- U55 -tan 'and those with him' vs U37 / U9 -ten 'those having': wording differs but the glossary treats -tan/-ten alike (qalqatan, aγta-tan); not harmonised further.
- U53 edün 'these' (Ming 這些每): a sense 'this many' is possible in Mongolian; no evidence in the text, left as the Ming has it.
- U5 i 'will you not stay as elders over all of these?': 'over' is a reading of aqalažu + accusative; kept, the note says what the text does not say.
- U7 'Heaven and Earth add strength to us': the dative γažar-a and 'to us' are the drafter's compromise; the note states both. Kept.
- U10 'each to his own place' (žüg žüg): žüg 'side, place' makes it defensible; only the tense was corrected.
- U29 morph odčuγ̇ui gloss says Ming 去了來 'went' while the note says 'went and came': cosmetic; left.
- U3 'a tail' vs 'the tail', U60 note 'they pour' vs i 'you pour': wording only; left.
- Many morph glosses repeat the Ming inside the gloss and in the bracket (e.g. 'whip (Ming 鞭子) [鞭子]'): cosmetic, left.
- U40 note 'The thirteen rings of tents are Chinggis's thirteen hosts…': an interpretation stated flatly; left, it is historical context and does not touch the grammar.
- U1 / U3 i drop the že particle ('indeed'): the particle's force is the glossary's 'indeed, so'; leaving it out of i is a smoothing choice, not an error.

## Main doubts left in the draft

- §125 speeches (U8–U9): nököčešü, boluγ̇užai, ülü-ü aqun ta: three endings with no secure analysis; the sense of the appeal (who is to be 'companions' to whom) rests on the Ming alone.
- U31 deġermedčü: passive only in the Ming (被); l gives the active form, i the Ming's passive.
- U46 qariγuluγ̇ad: accusative of Jamuqa + causative gives 'Jamuqa sent back', with no stated agent; the sentence's logic is unclear.
- U38 aisai and U60 tüsürüjü: endings unanalysed; U13 na: unknown force.
- U56 bolun 'all together': converb with the Ming 共, uncertain.
- U63 min-u jaγ̇un: 'what is mine?' is a reading of a lament, force uncertain.
- Names: Daγai/Taγai; Külelkü/Kürelkü; Qujuldar's vowels; the three-part Neġüdei-Čaγaγ̇an-Uγ̇a.
